name: Monomem
description: Self-hosted shared memory for AI coding agents: one SQLite file on the user's machine, shared by every connected tool. Each note carries a server-stamped writer, version history and undo. Reads and ordinary saves keep Guard's usual handling; forgetting, replacing, merging, purging history, changing trust or quarantine, and queueing or approving tasks are gated on review. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: No model is called and data stays in the local SQLite file. Semantic search is off by default; if MONOMEM_EMBEDDINGS is turned on and MONOMEM_EMBED_URL points at a remote host, note and search text are sent there.

A default install registers nine tools (state_write, state_read, state_search, state_list, state_delete, catch_up and the supersede preview/confirm/undo trio). The rest appear only when MONOMEM_TOOLS opts them in.

This stdio launch runs as the local operator with no token: every write is stamped written_by "stdio" and clients sharing it are not told apart. Scoped per-agent tokens apply only to the HTTP server (monomem serve), not here.
Over stdio the operator tools (memory_quarantine, trust_policy, memory_history_purge, memory_consolidate, task_approve) are refused unless MONOMEM_STDIO_ADMIN_TOOLS=1.

Under the default MONOMEM_LINT policy, known secret formats are refused and injection-like text is held for review; bare high-entropy strings are stored with a warning. MONOMEM_LINT=warn stores all of these, so this holds only by default.

state_delete is a logical delete: the note is hidden from every agent read and can be restored. Its text can remain in the database file, the WAL and backups; permanent removal is the operator CLI (monomem delete). It stays on review.

Replacing a note is preview then confirm, and memory_supersede_undo reverses it. task_put can queue a command task for a separately run, unpublished runner and task_approve lets it run; both stay on review.

This entry matches the monomem-mcp command (npm i -g monomem, 1.3.1 or later), which starts only the stdio MCP server. Launches such as npx -y monomem mcp, node <path>/cli.js mcp or cmd /c npx keep Guard normal handling.
